plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked carbohydrate enzyme & colonocyte energy chart from Xu et al. & Gordon (28 March 2003, Science 299: 2074–2076) and Turnbaugh, Ley & Gordon (21 December 2006, Nature 444: 1027–1031) compares the human genome's ~17 digestive glycoside hydrolases against Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron's 261 glycoside hydrolases (and thousands across the whole microbiome), converting dietary plant fibre into short-chain fatty acids (butyrate, propionate, acetate) that supply 60–70% of colon cell energy.
